subject: Discovery recap: Reliability & graceful degradation
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Jul 2026 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery call - reliability / graceful degradation (recap)

Thanks for taking the call today — really helpful to walk through our environment. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying items.

Pain points we described:
- Multiple recent incidents where upstream model latency spiked and requests timed out; customers saw 5–20% error rate during incidents.
- No automated failover across regions; when the primary region had issues we had to manually route traffic.
- Current vendor doesn’t offer a clear fallback model strategy (only one large model) so cost and latency balloon during outages.

Current stack/context:
- Ingest + inference runs in our k8s clusters (GKE) across us-west1 and us-east1.
- We host stateful caching via Redis in each region; KV cache is regional and not replicated.
- Use 2 vendor-managed models today, no dedicated capacity.

Success criteria for us:
- 99.9% availability for inference endpoints, p95 latency <150ms, p99 <500ms (for our standard chat flows).
- Automatic graceful degradation to a cheaper/quantized model with capped latency and clear error budget handling.
- Failover across regions with minimal manual ops and clear audit logs for incident RCA.

Next steps we asked for:
1) High-level doc on Redwood’s graceful degradation / fallback strategies and examples.
2) SOC 2 / compliance artifacts you can share.
3) Technical deep-dive with your infra lead to validate KV/cache behavior during failover.
4) A mutual action plan and proposed pilot timeline (2–4 week sandbox + canary).

I attached an incident timeline we exported from our monitoring for context: initial_incident_timeline.pdf (sample, redacted).

Thanks — John
John Doe
Head of Platform Engineering, Acme Inc
john.doe@acme.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call - reliability / graceful degradation (recap)

John — thanks for the thorough recap and for sharing the incident timeline, that was really helpful.

Confirming the points you listed and next steps from Redwood:
- We can meet your availability targets with a combination of Dedicated pools + automated routing/fallback policies. Our typical SLA for Dedicated customers can reach 99.95% uptime depending on commit; we'll include options in the MAP.
- Graceful degradation patterns we use: (1) route to warm quantized model variant, (2) fall back to regional replica, (3) if cross-region unavailable, fall back to a queued/lightweight response with an informative user-facing message. We’ll document trade-offs for latency vs quality.
- For KV cache: we’ll propose an approach that uses regional caches with optional cross-region replication/async warming to preserve cold-starts during failovers.

Deliverables we’ll send by EOD tomorrow:
1) RINF_SOC2_summary.pdf — high-level SOC 2 artifacts and compliance summary.
2) A short fallback_design_draft.pdf showing the routing/fallback flow and canary plan.
3) Proposed mutual action plan + pilot timeline link (shared in a follow-up).

Proposed next meeting: Technical deep-dive with Jonas (infra) and your platform team — Wed Jul 14, 10:00 AM PT? If that works I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior AE, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment: RINF_SOC2_summary.pdf

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: John Doe <john.doe@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jul 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery call - reliability / graceful degradation (recap)

John — quick technical follow-ups before the deep-dive so we can prepare:

1) KV cache model: are your Redis instances configured with persistence (AOF/RDB) today, or are they purely in-memory? If purely in-memory, we’ll treat cold-starts as expected and include warming strategies.

2) During the incidents you shared, were you hitting GPU provisioning limits or model OOMs, or was it primarily network/latency related? The difference changes whether we recommend Dedicated pools or regional autoscaling with burst capacity.

3) Are there any regulatory constraints that would prevent cross-region failover (data residency)?

Quick notes on options we’ll present in the deep-dive:
- Fallback models: we typically maintain a quantized 8-bit variant that can serve at lower cost and lower memory. That model is trained to prioritize core intent preservation; it’s used for graceful degradation during overloads.
- Routing policy: request router evaluates latency/cost/health and can route to (a) primary model instance, (b) regional replica, (c) quantized fallback. Policies are configurable per-route and per-customer.
- Canary & rollback plan: we’ll propose a canary that routes 5–10% of traffic to the new routing policy for 24–48 hours, with automated rollback on SLO breach.
- Observability: token-level latency and error breakdowns, per-route tracing, and alerting tied to your SLOs.

I attached a short draft diagram to illustrate the fallback flow: fallback_design_draft.pdf. Please send answers to the three questions above and we’ll tailor the deep-dive.

— Jonas
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Thanks Marissa/Jonas — Wed Jul 14 10:00 AM PT works for our team.

Answers to Jonas’ quick questions:
- Redis is configured with RDB snapshots but not AOF; cache is regional only.
- Incidents were a mix: a GPU OOM for one incident and network latency spikes for two others.
- No hard data residency blockers for cross-region failover, but we need audit trails.

I’ll upload additional logs to the Drive folder and attach a redacted incident log for your review: incident_log_excerpt.zip

Looking forward to the deep-dive.

— John
